issues: Covers fell by 12 (1%) to 1,182 week on week while spend per head rose by £0.34 (1.63%) to £21.16; 103 guests came from the hotel app on Sunday between 12pm and 3pm at 15% off.
Sales were £25,586.23, down £10.57 (0.04%) week on week and £2,086.22 (8.88%) above the £23,500 target.
The report puts potential revenue at a further £4,750.06; sales are capping at around £25K and extra labour will be used to send out flyers.
SPH was held back by free ramen, £5 ramen and SLL offers, and the 50% SLL offer brings down the sales number.
Wage cost was 28.45% and food cost 27.86%; adjusted for discounts (£30,000 total sales including £4,500 of discounts against £7,280 of labour), labour is 24% rather than 28%.
Food and drinks variance was 2% (food 2.0%, wet 2.2%), and the head chef puts actual food cost at a normal 23% to 24%.
Labour notes: hiring continues, more hours are going into training, BOH could not take two hour breaks because of prep, and more FOH is needed because the site is busy.
Saturday sales have surged from around £2.7K to £4K to £5K (£4.5K last week and £4.4K the week before) because of B2B partnerships, hotel apps and app advertising.

Only two staff were rostered for Saturday lunch and four for dinner because the rota was based on historical sales intervals, which caused service problems; Ziang Lin said past intervals reflect past constraints rather than true potential.
App push notifications and theatre promotions bring sudden surges, with app bookings made only about 10 minutes ahead, and the heaviest surge is between 5pm and 7pm.
The Friday rota of 54 hours for £4.6K of sales is too low and would run at an unsustainable 16% labour.
Thursday lunches need extra support for large office bookings of 15 to 20 people.
Service must hold up to avoid partner hotels such as Hilton removing the site from their apps, with potential revenue growth from £30K to £40K to £45K a week if performance holds.
Ziang Lin will be based mainly at Shoreditch from 07/10, with Kaitlin Docherty on Wednesday and Thursday, and a team member from M7 will work 25 hours a week to support the site.
Google reviews: the report shows a 5.00 rating for the week, and the meeting recorded 65 five star, 4 four star and 2 one star reviews, with a 4.8 lifetime average from over 500 reviews.
The two 1 star reviews were for cold vegetable gyoza and a 45 minute wait for chicken katsu curry during an unexpected rush; the head chef attributed them to FOH customer handling.
On Wednesday 30/09 a customer found plastic in a California roll.
On Wednesday 30/09 chicken katsu was 30 minutes late because a 16 cover table delayed walk ins, and four lunch deals were comped; the cold gyoza complaint was confirmed when tasted.
Naveen drives the site's Google reviews (over 60) and will take on daily compliance checks and review collection.
Mahek handles stock takes well and is continuing inventory training to complete them independently.
Aashish has joined BOH from O2, Ashika is to be used more on sides and ramen rather than KP, and the site will keep hiring a sushi chef and FOH.
A new BOH starter is due on Monday, pending HR confirmation.
Sushi cover is thin: the head chef asked for two weeks of sushi training for backup, Razak can support from Soho, and Sophie and Srawut want a potential leader rather than temporary cover.
Double ordering (for example chilli beans and thick noodles) is to be stopped by reviewing pending orders before placing new ones, and food ordering is restricted to £200.

Areas for improvement: inconsistent upselling and Irasshaimase, slow service because the section plan was not followed, only one person responsible for Deliveroo per shift, and the need for one more bill ticket printer at the sushi side or hot section pass.

New kitchen rules: from Monday to Wednesday one person breaks 2:30pm to 4:30pm and another 3pm to 5pm, the sushi chef helps BOH prep from 2pm to 3pm, chefs must not refuse orders after last orders or close without checking with the manager in charge, and the closing manager checks kitchen hygiene.
Menu and supply changes: no crème brûlée or brownie, a change of supplier for steak tataki and sous vide chicken, and yakisoba timing changed from 1:20 to 1:50.
The dishwasher constantly produces bubbles and the women's toilet light needs fixing; the filter needs a deep clean and leaks are being managed with buckets.
Pest control was completed on 22/09 and fire safety, electrical, gas and ventilation had no issues.
TownHall events run every weekend, and an influencer is collecting frozen ramen on 12/10.
Local B2B outreach for the 15% staff discount programme continued around Shoreditch, including hotels and workplaces.
At the 07/10 AM Updates meeting, Teddy Lee recommended a panic button protocol so extra help can be called in during unexpected busy periods such as Saturdays.
Region-wide (South, AM Updates 07/10): every site is targeted to reach a 4.5 star delivery rating.
